title: Childhood brain tumours and use of mobile phones: comparison of a case-control study with incidence data.
ehr_evidence: Rates are shown for the age group 5 –19 years living in the Nordic Countries obtained from NORDCAN
summary: Commentary responding to a previous critique, arguing that stable childhood brain tumour incidence trends in the Nordic countries are inconsistent with the increased risk suggested by the CEFALO case-control study on mobile phone use.
key_findings: Commentary presents no new primary quantitative results; argues that stable childhood brain tumour incidence trends in the Nordic countries over the last 20 years are inconsistent with the increased risk suggested by the CEFALO case-control study.
population: children and adolescents aged 5-19 years in the Nordic countries
limitations: reliance on retrospective self-reported exposure in the referenced case-control study
potential age-specific underreporting in cancer registry data
